record.original_question: LetS W n be the set of permutations ofnordered by the weak Bruhat order. Characterize the intervals ofS W n that are distributive lattices and compute their total number. The values for 1≤n≤8 are 1, 2, 16, 124, 1262, 15898, 238572, 4152172.

evidence.quote: [Stan2012, Ch. 3 Exer. 185(j)] LetS W n be the set of permutations ofnordered by the weak Bruhat order. Characterize the intervals ofS W n that are distributive lattices and compute their total number. The values for 1≤n≤8 are 1, 2, 16, 124, 1262, 15898, 238572, 4152172.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters, equipped with the (right) weak Bruhat order: for $u,v \in S_n$, set $u \le v$ iff there exists a reduced expression of $v$ that has a reduced expression of $u$ as a prefix, equivalently $\ell(v) = \ell(u) + \ell(u^{-1}v)$ where $\ell$ denotes the Coxeter length (number of inversions). For $u \le v$, the interval $[u,v] = \{w \in S_n : u \le w \le v\}$ inherits a lattice structure from the weak order.

(a) Give an explicit combinatorial characterization of those pairs $(u,v)$ with $u \le v$ in $S_n$ such that the weak order interval $[u,v]$ is a distributive lattice.

(b) Compute, as a function of $n$, the total number $d(n)$ of such intervals (i.e., the number of pairs $(u,v)$ with $u \le v$ and $[u,v]$ distributive). The known initial values for $1 \le n \le 8$ are
$$1,\ 2,\ 16,\ 124,\ 1262,\ 15898,\ 238572,\ 4152172.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in Stanley's Enumerative Combinatorics (Ch. 3, Exercise 185(j)) as an open question. Related work refines weak order intervals into distributive lattices (Hersh–Mészáros, 2013) and studies a "middle order" between weak and Bruhat that is always a distributive lattice (Bouvel–Ferrari–Tenner, 2024), but no closed-form characterization of all distributive weak-order intervals or formula for their count is known.

status_evidence.title: A refinement of weak order intervals into distributive lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Refines arbitrary weak-order intervals into distributive lattices via Lehmer codes.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not characterize which intervals are themselves distributive.

status_evidence.title: Between weak and Bruhat: the middle order on permutations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies a middle order between weak and Bruhat orders that is a distributive lattice.
status_evidence.claim: Related distributive structure on permutations, distinct from the open characterization.
